correspondence.component_scope: Chosen upper Buffalo Creek opening and westward mountain ravine
correspondence.finding: The chosen eastern opening lies on the directly labeled Buffalo Creek in the southern Desatoya mountain setting. The original maps depict the westward ravine and its turn into the north-trending Buffalo Creek valley. The chosen initial bends remain in this same mapped stream corridor.
correspondence.name_scope: Buffalo Creek is a directly supported bounded upper-reach name. No claim is made that the selected first point is the complete natural river source.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward Buffalo Creek corridor and tributary entries
correspondence.finding: The selected route turns north between the East Gate Range and the Desatoya side, following the connected Buffalo Creek channel and its valley floor. The maps cover the Road Canyon Creek entry and the approach to the Big Den Creek join. The eastern tributary headwaters are separate from the selected southern opening.
correspondence.name_scope: Repeated Buffalo Creek labels follow this bounded upper corridor. Road Canyon Creek and Big Den Creek are joining tributary context, not alternative names for the selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Buffalo Creek to Eastgate Wash westward turn and Rock Creek receiving junction
correspondence.finding: Past the Big Den Creek junction, the selected corridor turns west through the Eastgate passage into the directly labeled Eastgate Wash. The wash continues west across the northern part of the open Eastgate floor and meets the Rock Creek approach near the highway, then bends southwest along the receiving wash. The enclosing passage and connected blue linework support the selected joins at ordinary corridor scale.
correspondence.name_scope: Buffalo Creek and Eastgate Wash are distinct bounded reach identities. Rock Creek is tributary context rather than the selected opening.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastgate Wash western floor, Bench Creek join and highway-side narrows
correspondence.finding: The original maps continue Eastgate Wash westward along the highway corridor, past the Bench Creek entry and through the narrow low passage between adjacent uplands. The selected generalized bends are covered on both scales. The southern distributary channels and separate southern valley floor are not substituted for this selected westward wash.
correspondence.name_scope: Eastgate Wash is directly labeled on the selected western receiving reach. Bench Creek names the northern joining branch.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastgate Wash outlet into Dixie Valley Wash and northward turn
correspondence.finding: The selected wash passes west out of the highway-side narrows and turns north around the western foot of Chalk Mountain. Repeated Dixie Valley Wash labels follow the receiving channel from this outlet into the southern Dixie Valley corridor. The Wonder Wash tributary entry is mapped along the northward continuation.
correspondence.name_scope: Dixie Valley Wash is directly supported on the selected receiving trunk; Wonder Wash is a separate eastern tributary. Different upper reach names do not prevent this representative receiving-system identity.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern Dixie Valley Wash, Elevenmile Wash entry and elongated alluvial corridor
correspondence.finding: The selection continues north along the mapped Dixie Valley Wash beside the southern mountain fronts. The middle original covers the Elevenmile Wash entry from the west, the narrow axial section and its opening into the broader valley floor. Repeated channel labels and the enclosing low wash corridor support ordinary continuous correspondence.
correspondence.name_scope: Dixie Valley Wash names the selected receiving trunk. Elevenmile Wash is a joining tributary, not the selected mainstem.

correspondence.component_scope: Central Dixie Valley axial floor, elongated sediment patches and Cattle Road crossing
correspondence.finding: The route continues along the same north-trending low valley floor through elongated sediment patches, local roads and the Cattle Road setting. The named intermittent channel runs within this continuous axial receiving corridor. Generalized selected positions sometimes lie beside the fine mapped channel line, but remain in the same receiving floor without a separate basin transfer.
correspondence.name_scope: Dixie Valley Wash remains the receiving-system identity. Individual sediment patches, small ponds and road-side drains are not given new river names.

correspondence.component_scope: Dixie Valley settlement-area continuation and northeastward bend
correspondence.finding: The selected route passes north through the mapped settlement-road grid and bends northeast with the lower Dixie Valley Wash corridor. The terminal detail distinguishes the labeled wash from nearby straight drainage lines, small ponds and local roads. Ordinary corridor correspondence is continuous through this developed lowland setting; no particular ditch operation is asserted.
correspondence.name_scope: Dixie Valley Wash is directly labeled on the lower receiving corridor. Dixie Valley settlement labels are not treated as hydronyms.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower wash termination and continuous Humboldt Salt Marsh receiving floor
correspondence.finding: The selected route continues northeast from the labeled lower wash across the same open low receiving floor toward the southern margin of Humboldt Salt Marsh. Both map scales continuously cover this wash-to-playa approach, with no intervening ridge or separate closed-basin transfer. A blue channel is not drawn through every dry patch, and no currently wetted thread is required or inferred.
correspondence.name_scope: The wash name is bounded to its mapped stream corridor; Humboldt Salt Marsh names the distinct terminal receiving feature.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern Humboldt Salt Marsh entry and interior passage
correspondence.finding: The route crosses the southern irregular margin of the mapped Humboldt Salt Marsh and continues northeast within the same broad salt-marsh/playa body. The original cartography continuously covers the entry, bends and receiving interior. The distinct pond and spring settings to the west are not substituted for the selected terminal feature.
correspondence.name_scope: Humboldt Salt Marsh is a directly labeled receiving marsh/playa, not a scalar river name.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected endpoint inside Humboldt Salt Marsh
correspondence.finding: The last selected bends and actual endpoint lie within the interior of the directly labeled Humboldt Salt Marsh, beyond its southern entry. The endpoint does not represent the full northern limit of the mapped marsh. Both original map scales cover the endpoint setting.
correspondence.name_scope: Humboldt Salt Marsh is the actual terminal receiving feature. Dixie Valley Wash is the representative receiving-system identity rather than a name imposed on the marsh interior.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen western headward feeder and Boston Creek entry
correspondence.finding: The upper original depicts a small eastward feeder from the chosen opening, joining the larger north- and east-turning watercourse labeled Boston Creek. The opening and immediate joining drainage are distinguishable from the separate southern Boston headward arm. Generalized positions are used to identify the valley, not individual banks.
correspondence.name_scope: The initial feeder has no separately established name; Boston Creek applies to the receiving named component.

correspondence.component_scope: Boston Creek upper bend, southward mountain valley and entry to McCarthy Marsh
correspondence.finding: Repeated Boston Creek labels follow the eastward bend and southward valley. The source depicts side-stream joins, the Baker Creek entry and the meandering Boston corridor continuing onto the pond-rich lowland. Off-channel ponds and McCarthy Marsh retain their own setting and are not renamed Boston Creek.
correspondence.name_scope: Boston Creek is directly supported for the named upper river component; Baker Creek is a distinct entering tributary.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected Boston Creek to Pargon-side feeder transfer across McCarthy Marsh
correspondence.finding: The selected corridor leaves the mapped eastward-turning Boston Creek belt and passes south across a pond-patterned interbranch flat toward a small mapped tributary entering Pargon River. The topographic original shows that southern feeder and its Pargon connection, but not its through-connection to Boston Creek. The independent photographic original likewise distinguishes the Boston and Pargon meander belts and intervening ponds/vegetated channels without establishing this selected direct transfer. Pargon and Fish meet in the downstream receiving setting. This is an unresolved interbranch connection, not a demand for a continuously wetted thread, precise bank, present overflow or operating-condition proof.
correspondence.name_scope: Boston Creek and Pargon River are separate directly labeled components. Neither basin proximity nor the model connects them as the selected through-route.

correspondence.component_scope: Fish River receiving valley, southwestward confined reach and Niukluk junction
correspondence.finding: The overview and middle original depict the Fish River receiving trunk below the marsh tributary setting, its southwestward confined valley, side-creek junctions and the opening toward the Niukluk River confluence. Repeated Fish River labels and continuous mapped valley/channel establish this downstream component. The shared stage-3/stage-2 boundary remains within that same receiving river setting.
correspondence.name_scope: Fish River is supported as the downstream receiving river; Niukluk River is a distinct entering tributary, not a whole-feature alias.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Fish River below Niukluk and approach to White Mountain
correspondence.finding: The lower original continuously depicts the broad, looping Fish River below the Niukluk junction, its connected sloughs and the wetland approach to White Mountain. The fragment boundary is a display-stage split, with ordinary geographic river continuity supported independently by the source.
correspondence.name_scope: Fish River is directly labeled; nearby sloughs and ponds are not separately assigned a scalar river name.

correspondence.component_scope: White Mountain and interconnected western delta channels
correspondence.finding: The lower original distinguishes Fish River at White Mountain, the western Klokerblok River branch and the eastern Mudyutok River branch. Connected channel lines tie the selected western delta corridor into the lower Fish channel. The branching delta setting supports ordinary correspondence without choosing a current active distributary or matching each generalized position to a bank.
correspondence.name_scope: Fish River and Klokerblok River are separate mapped delta names; Mudyutok River is the distinguishable eastern branch, not the selected whole-feature name.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower delta, distinct source/render endpoints and actual lagoon receiving setting
correspondence.finding: The supplied source endpoint and later rendered endpoint are distinct. Both lie in the lower Fish delta/shore-approach setting represented in the map; neither is substituted for a surveyed mouth. The cartography depicts the connected lower Fish channels entering Golovnin Lagoon. The generalized rendered end does not establish an exact present shoreline, and the actual lagoon receiver is recorded separately from the river and its delta.
correspondence.name_scope: Fish River is the named terminal river component; Golovnin Lagoon is the distinct coastal receiving waterbody.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestern selected opening and northward upper-river approach
correspondence.finding: Santa Maria do Pará original depicts the selected southern stream corridor continuing north into the labelled Maracanã along the western side of the municipal setting. The upper imagery independently shows its continuous wooded drainage ribbon amid cultivated land and its northeastward continuation. The initial stored point is not asserted to be the named river’s natural spring.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper and middle Maracanã to the selected tributary junction
correspondence.finding: The mapped Maracanã runs northeast past the Prata/Porto Nazaré setting, then north through the Livramento and Nova Timboteua western-border corridor to Porto Seguro. Repeated river labels and continuous mapped channel/wetland linework correspond with the supplied sequence. Joining Jeju/Taciateua and smaller igarapés remain joining-water context, not separate selected mainstem names. Imagery confirms one meandering floodplain corridor; generalized stored segments cutting across meander lobes are not treated as separate transfers.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern tributary opening and junction near Porto Seguro
correspondence.finding: Nova Timboteua original directly labels the eastern meandering watercourse Rio Peixe Boi and depicts its uninterrupted joining connection with the Maracanã at the western side of the Boa Vista/Porto Seguro setting. The complete selected short tributary, including its initial eastern part and terminal confluence, lies in this mapped and photographed corridor. Its label is retained as a component name, not a whole-system alias.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Maracanã past Santarém Novo into the broad coastal river
correspondence.finding: The first stage1 part continues directly downstream from the stage3 mainstem and tributary junction. Municipal mapping follows successive broad river bends past Santarém Novo, through the wetland and mangrove-margin setting into the widening channel east of Maracanã town. Imagery corroborates the same bends, small islands and lateral channels without a missing cross-basin or managed through-link.

correspondence.component_scope: Inner estuarine bend beside Maracanã town
correspondence.finding: The selected mainstem ends at the broad west-turning estuarine reach beside Maracanã town. The original directly prints Rio Maracanã on this watercourse and depicts its open receiving connection farther north; imagery shows the same widening and islands. The final generalized westward display segment approaches the mangrove-side receiving margin. This is the actual selected endpoint setting, not a claim that the selection extends to the open Atlantic shoreline or precisely follows a surveyed bank.

correspondence.component_scope: chosen opening and southern feeder
correspondence.finding: The chosen southwestern opening and eastward feeder lie in the wet coastal-plain lowland feeding the southern Nanni setting. Imagery shows continuous vegetated wetland terrain; the study maps and field description place this in the old/young coastal-plain transition. No local channel name is assigned and no continuously exposed wet thread is required.

correspondence.component_scope: southern wetland northward passage
correspondence.finding: All selected northward parts remain within the same broad forested and open-swamp receiving corridor east of the separate Corantijn Canal. Sparse open water and vegetation concealment do not themselves create an unsupported transfer. Corantijn Canal is contextual and is not assigned as the selected reach.

correspondence.component_scope: nanni eastern bend and ridge passage
correspondence.finding: The eastward bend and turn toward the northern swamp correspond to the Nanni corridor across the ridge/swamp setting shown in the field-study mapping. The study specifically addresses the vegetated creek and swamp passages. Adjacent Camisa/Blackawatra tributary labels are not treated as whole-system names.

correspondence.component_scope: northern nanni swamp to polder margin
correspondence.finding: The northern swamp passage and approach to the Nanni works follow the mapped Nanni Creek corridor. Geographic continuity through the vegetated basin is supported; present discharge and exact open-water alignment are unclaimed.

correspondence.component_scope: nanni managed junction
correspondence.finding: The selected path reaches the dam/intake and polder-margin setting. The sources expressly distinguish the natural lower Nanni route west to Corantijn from the managed Van Wouw diversion north into the rice area. The selected path takes the latter geographic corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: van wouw side corridor
correspondence.finding: The northwest approach within the western polder canal setting corresponds at ordinary corridor scale to the Van Wouw-side managed route. This establishes a bounded constructed reach, not a natural-river name for the downstream agricultural network.

correspondence.component_scope: final cross polder transfer
correspondence.finding: The selected final part leaves the supported Van Wouw-side route and traverses separate western polder field/drain compartments toward the sea dike. The inspected maps do not establish this particular transfer into the coastal drain/outfall; imagery shows compartments and multiple channels but does not resolve the selected through-link. This is the single remaining material gap, not a demand for current gate operations or exact banks.

correspondence.component_scope: actual endpoint receiving setting
correspondence.finding: The actual selected endpoint is on the outer Corantijn estuary coast along the western-polder sea dike, southwest of Nieuw Nickerie. Its receiving shoreline setting is visible. It is distinct from the mapped natural Nanni Creek mouth farther south; no named sluice is assigned from proximity alone.
